A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CrossOver. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary sections A–I are available and support reliable comparison; the shorter v2 reflects reformatting rather than missing material.

before.justification: V1 reports original instance and scene retrieval experiments on ScanNet and 3RScan, alongside ablations, localization evaluations, qualitative examples, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results in the main paper and supplementary material.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.5 retain the same instance encoders, scene fusion, unified dimensionality encoders, contrastive losses, missing-modality masking, and retrieval procedure. The wording edits do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use ScanNet and 3RScan, with the same SceneVerse referrals and Scan2CAD/ShapeNet resources. Instance retrieval, scene retrieval, temporal matching, missing-modality scenarios, and supplementary localization coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: ULIP-2, PointBind, and the instance baseline remain in their corresponding retrieval comparisons; temporal matching and Appendix E retain their original comparator sets.

E3.justification: The validation splits, recall metrics and thresholds, modality-availability splits, camera-view settings, and training budgets are unchanged. Renumbered experimental subsections and relocated tables do not introduce new protocols.

E4.justification: Table 4 and Appendices A–I retain the same missing-modality, data-scaling, all-pairs training, encoder-input, camera-count, runtime, and qualitative success/failure analyses. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including Appendix H's runtime measurement of 1.01 ± 0.26 seconds. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance testing for retrieval performance.

E6.justification: The tabulated values, plotted curves, and qualitative retrieval examples are retained. For example, Table 1 preserves CrossOver's 92.31/84.62/57.69 temporal matching recalls. The ScanNet and 3RScan retrieval tables exchange numbering without changing results.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 and Appendix I's spatial-relationship definitions are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises theoretical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about flexible scene-level alignment, dimensionality-specific encoders, three-stage training, and emergent cross-modal behavior.

C2.justification: V1 Section 4.4 says the method surpasses its instance baseline 'in most cases'; v2 Section 4.2 drops that qualification. This makes the interpretation less precise because unchanged Figure 6 still favors the baseline for image-to-text top-20 retrieval. Other explanations and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices G–I retain the camera-sampling procedure, hardware, runtime, 768-dimensional embeddings, 300-epoch training, optimizer, learning rate, and freezing details. The project-link target is also unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 48 cited works and related-work positioning are retained. Reference 34 gains fuller SGAligner publication metadata, but this does not introduce a new citation or change the relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: V2 shortens several method and experiment passages, converts the dataset and metric subsections into run-in headings, and renumbers subsequent subsections. Author affiliations and bibliographic metadata are updated; the overall narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: Existing figures and tables are resized or relocated, particularly Figures 5–6 and Tables 1–4. Tables 2–3 exchange numbering, and page numbers are added. These are layout adjustments preserving the existing display designs and content.

improvement.justification: V2 mainly compacts the layout and makes small editorial corrections while preserving the method, empirical evidence, and appendix details. These limited presentation gains accompany a less qualified baseline comparison in Section 4.2. Together, the changes leave overall paper quality essentially unchanged.
